the opt-in fragment WORD_WND_RULES (WORD_WN_RULES plus one-way N∘D→D∘N and the exact sign-flips N∘Ip→Im∘N, N∘Im→Ip∘N) is terminating and locally confluent; every word has a unique syntactic normal form

the balanced Monna map B(sum a_i 3^i)=sum a_i 3^{-i-1} with a_i in {-1,0,+1} is an affine conjugate of Monna's 1952 digit-reversal map; the residual graph recursion Gamma_F is the existing residual Mealy machine, not a new dynamical invariant

for every balanced-Monna endpoint pair u=zeta+2*3^n, v=zeta-2*3^n one has u^3-v^3=4*3^n(3 zeta^2+4*3^{2n}) and therefore t=v_3(u^3-v^3)=n+min(1+2 v_3(zeta), 2n), or t=3n when zeta=0; the two arguments of the minimum have opposite parity whenever zeta is nonzero
the cubic divergence-depth spectrum at level n=0 is two pairs of depth 0; for n>=1, depth 3n occurs twice and depth n+1+2s occurs 4*3^{n-s-1} times for each 0<=s<n
cubing never sends a balanced-Monna endpoint pair to an endpoint pair: 3 zeta^2+4*3^{2n} is never +/- 3^k, so u^3-v^3 is never +/- 4*3^k and B(u^3)=B(v^3) never holds
the next-state output D(x+y) is not D-local: there is no G such that D(x+y)=G(D(x),D(y)) for all x,y; witness D(0+0)=0 and D(1+1)=1 while D(0)=D(1)=0

for U,V,W in {S,I+,I-,N}, the identity U(x)+V(y)=W(x+y) holds for all integers iff it is one of the eight concrete triples (S,S,S), (N,N,N), (I+,S,I+), (S,I+,I+), (I-,S,I-), (S,I-,I-), (I+,I-,S), (I-,I+,S); same-sign I+ or I- and mixed N+S are not constructor identities

the named carry-free push-in system (unary D(S(t))→t plus S(Add(t,u))→Add(S(t),S(u)) and congruence, no D-through-Add) is not locally confluent: D(S(Add(X,Y))) has two distinct irreducibles Add(X,Y) and D(Add(S(X),S(Y))); both evaluate to X+Y

the packaged Add boundary combines three exact statements: D(x+y) is not D-local, same-sign I_a is not a constructor identity, and the named carry-free S-through-Add push-in extension fails local confluence
for Γ_NP, if n > 0 and n is not 0 or 12 mod 24, then the kernel family state t_n = (q_{n-1}, -q_{n-2}, 0) is not origin-reachable under unrestricted integer steps T_w

for Γ_NP, the unread-tail energy E_i(s) = s1 q_{i-2} + s2 q_{i-1} + s3 q_i (with q_j = 0 for j < 0) satisfies E_{i-1}(T_w s) = E_i(s) - w q_{i-1} for i ≥ 1, equivalently the adjoint covariance u_{i-1} A = u_i

for Γ_NP, after an MSD word w of length k from remaining n+k, the unread-tail energy satisfies E_n(T_w s) = E_{n+k}(s) - sum_j w_j q_{n+k-1-j}; this is the cumulative form of energy_step, not a bound on L_0

for Γ_NP, the set of integer controls w such that E_{n-1}(T_w s) lies in a fixed integer interval [lo, hi] is consecutive: if w1 and w2 satisfy the bounds and w1 ≤ w ≤ w2 then w does too; this is energy_step plus q>0, not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, homogeneous residual motion is energy-neutral in the sliding index: E_n(A^k s) = E_{n+k}(s), equivalently energy_telescope on the zero word; this is not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP and n≥2, the determinant of consecutive adjoints (u_n, u_{n-1}, u_{n-2}) equals 3^{n-2}, so neighboring energies invert s over Q; this is not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, from the origin an MSD word ws unfolds by variation of constants: foldSteps ws origin equals the particular sum −∑ A^{k-1-j} e3 w_j; this is not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, the origin impulse A^r e3 equals (3 q_{r-1}, 3 q_{r-2}+q_{r-1}, q_r) with q_j=0 for j<0; this is the place-value dictionary for origin_particular, not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, the MSD recurrence word B*=(1,-2,-1,-3) has consumed sum zero at every start remaining n+4: q_{n+3}-2q_{n+2}-q_{n+1}-3q_n=0; this is q_rec, not a bound on L_0

for Γ_NP, from the origin the third coordinate of the control particular equals minus the MSD consumed valuation: (particularSum ws)_3 = -consumedSum |ws| ws, so val(B)=0 iff c_B lies on F={s_3=0}; this is energy_telescope at n=0, not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, MSD consumed sum splits at two starts: consumedSum (n+|U|+|V|)(UV) = consumedSum (n+|U|+|V|)U + consumedSum (n+|V|)V; this is not val(U)+C val(V) and not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, complete-word concatenation satisfies val(UV)=val(V)-E_|V|(c_U), equivalently val(UV)=0 iff E_|V|(c_U)=val(V); this is particular_concat plus energy_homogeneous, not a bound on L_0
complete zero-value words form a monoid under concatenation: val(U)=val(V)=0 implies val(UV)=0
for Γ_NP, after an MSD word B from any residual s, (T_B(s))_3 = E_|B|(s) - val(B), so T_B(s) lies on F iff E_|B|(s)=val(B); this is energy_telescope at remaining 0, not a bound on L_0
on origin-live remaining-0 slices of Γ_NP a uniform unnormalized bound |z_j|≤C holds, equivalently infinite liveness forces all expanding companion modes bounded
for Γ_NP, the MSD word (B*)^k · (1,-2) has origin particular equal to the hub (-3,-1,0); this is the reset identity plus hub_nonreset, not a bound on L_0
arbitrarily long origin-accepted words of Γ_NP force infinitely many distinct remaining-0 terminals
for Γ_NP, if T_w(s)=t then s equals the integer reverse (t2-t1/3, t3+w-2 t1/3, t1/3); on F this is (b-a/3, w-2a/3, a/3). This is inversion of step, not a bound on L_0
origin-reachable remaining-0 terminals of Γ_NP satisfy a congruence on F strictly stronger than 3|a, equivalently 9|a or gcd of b-coordinates >1
for Γ_NP, if T_R(0)=0 then T_{RU}(0)=T_U(0); origin-reset prefixes do not create new terminals. This is particular_concat at c_R=0, not a bound on L_0
for Γ_NP, if E_|v|(s)=E_|v|(t) then T_v(s) lands on F iff T_v(t) does; length-n suffix acceptance is classified by E_n, not by residual coordinates. This is fold_on_F_iff, not a bound on L_0

for F(x)=x^2 and the infinite output language Y={0,+}^ω that never emits -1, the language L of trit words whose residual outputs of F all lie in {0,+} is not regular; equivalently the 3-adic preimage X=F^{-1}(Y) is not sofic. The prefixes 10^m are pairwise Myhill-Nerode inequivalent because the residual g_m(x)=3^{m+1}x^2+2x accepts w_m=(-1)^{m+1}0 while every g_n with n>m rejects it

for F(x)=x^2 write C_F(m,r) for the number of ≡_r classes among the unrestricted residuals of F at input depth m. Then C_F(m,r)=3^m whenever r≥m≥0, and C_F(m,m-1)=3^m-3 for every m≥2. The latter deficit is exactly three doubletons: for each σ in {-1,0,+1}, the two length-m extensions of σ^{m-1} by a trit other than σ are ≡_{m-1}-equivalent, and every other same-depth pair is distinguished

for F(x)=x^2 and r>=1, unrestricted ≡_r types at depth m>r inject into pairs (p mod 3^r, DZ^m(p^2) mod 3^r) for p in P_m. On the fibre p≡0 (mod 3^r): if m=2r the second coordinate runs exactly over the quadratic residues in Z/3^r Z, hence C_{x^2}(2r,r)<3^{2r}; if m>=3r the second coordinate is all of Z/3^r Z, via p=3^r + v 3^{m-r} for v in P_r. This decides the zero fibre, not C_{x^2}(m,r) for a general fibre. Cf. BTR-x2-C-band

for F(x)=x^2, r>=1 and m>=5r, every fibre p≡α (mod 3^r) of the interior map has second coordinate all of Z/3^r Z. Explicitly, for α,u in P_r the prefix p=α + u 3^r + 3^{m-r} lies in P_m, satisfies p≡α (mod 3^r), and DZ^m(p^2)≡2u + DZ^r(2α) (mod 3^r); the unit 2 makes u↦2u+const bijective. In particular no fibre stays incomplete for all m. This is not a first-saturation time of C_{x^2}(m,r). Cf. BTR-x2-C-interior
The LSD carry of normalizing the doubled trit stream 2 d_i, d_i in {-1,0,1}, stays in {-1,0,1}; 1 and -1 are reachable from 0.
V(c)=|c| strictly decreases under c |-> DZ(c+2d) whenever |c|>=2 and d is a trit.
Doubled-trit carry and output are odd: T(-c,-d)=-T(c,d) and the emitted trit negates.
The three carries -1,0,1 have pairwise distinct Mealy output signatures, so the 3-state machine is minimal.
The synthetic map T_3(c,d)=3 DZ(c+2d) satisfies c_n=3n along the all-+1 word, so the residual set is unbounded. This is not value-preserving normalization.
For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), lsd(T(n))=-lsd(n) and lsd(T^k(n))=(-1)^k lsd(n). Future LSD observations depend only on lsd(n).
Laboratory DZ is a left inverse of T: DZ(T(n))=n. Canonical T is the section I_{-lsd(n)}(n), not a constant-section I_a.
T(I_a(x))=9x+2a and lsd(T(I_a(x)))=-a, independent of the higher-digit residual x.
|T(n)| < |n| for all integers n, where T(n)=3n-lsd(n)
For T_λ(n)=3n-λ lsd(n), lsd(T_2(n))=lsd(n) and lsd(T_3(n))=0. The observational residual remains a trit; λ changes the residue map, not the need for the full integer.
For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), the length-2 integer jet satisfies J2(T(n))=(-lsd(n), lsd(n)). The map depends only on the first digit; every trit window (a,b) is sent to (-a,a).
The J2-orbit of T requires lsd(D^2(n)) or otherwise information beyond J2(n)
J2(T_2(n))=(lsd(n),0) and J2(T_3(n))=(0,0). Order-2 observation distinguishes T_2 from T, unlike the one-digit residual.

For T(n)=3n-lsd(n), the length-3 integer jet satisfies J3(T(n))=(-lsd(n), lsd(n), lsd(DZ(n))). Equivalently J3(T(n))=(-a,a,b) when J2(n)=(a,b). The third input digit is discarded. The map factors through J2.
J3(T(n)) is a function of lsd(n) alone
J3(T_2(n))=(lsd(n),0,lsd(DZ(n))) and J3(T_3(n))=(0,0,lsd(DZ(n))). T_3 collapses J1 and J2 but does not collapse J3: the second input digit survives.
D(x+y)=D(x)+D(y)+D(lsd(x)+lsd(y)). The missing state at the unary/Add boundary is D of the local digit sum.
D(x+y) is a function of (D(x), D(y), lsd(x+y))
If s,a,b are trits then D(s+a+b) is a trit. The streaming residual of trit addition is exactly {-1,0,1}. Three values occur on D(x)=D(y)=0, so the residual is minimal.
The shortcut map C(n)=n/2 (even) or (3n+1)/2 (odd) is well-defined on positive integers, and {1,2} is a 2-cycle.
V(n)=n strictly decreases on every shortcut step.
For every L≥1, n=2^L-1 realises L odd shortcut steps and C^L(n)=3^L-1>n. No residual n mod 2^L with blocks of length at most L certifies strict descent.
I_0(x)=3x. If |x|>1 then 3|x| is composite.
I_a(n) mod m depends only on n mod m.
The finite sieve residual gcd(n,210)=1 does not equal Prime: I_0(1)=3 is prime and I_0(211)=633 is composite, with 1≡211 (mod 210).
Equal length-L LSD jets have identical Prime continuation behaviour.
For λ=1 and |u|≤m, if |s|≤⌊m/2⌋ then |D(s+u)|≤⌊m/2⌋. The looser radius ⌈(m+1)/2⌉ from 3|D n|≤|n|+1 is not required.
For F_{λ,U_m}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u) and every integer λ≥0, a finite invariant box containing 0 exists if and only if λ≤2 or m≤1.
Gain λ=3 forces unbounded residual independently of the raw alphabet U.
For F_{2,U_2} the origin-reachable set is {-2,0,2} while the smallest invariant interval is [-2,2]. Interval invariance is not the reachable residual.
r-way trit addition s'=D(s+a_1+⋯+a_r) is F_{1,U_r}: a trit sum of length r has absolute value at most r, so the λ=1 box |s|≤⌊r/2⌋ is invariant. The count 2⌊r/2⌋+1 equals 1,3,3,5 for r=1,2,3,4.

If λ≥3 and |u|≥2 then the constant-control orbit of F_{λ,U} from 0 is unbounded: at λ=3 one has s'=s+u-lsd(s+u) so each step moves by at least 1; at λ≥4 the step is strictly expanding on the matching ray.
For λ=2 and |u|≤m, if |s|≤2 m.pred then |2 D(s+u)|≤2 m.pred. This is the sharp invariant radius 2(m-1)_+.
Holes or asymmetry in the raw alphabet U change the finite/infinite residual phase at fixed (λ, max|u|).
The minimal residual complexity M(λ,U) is determined by (λ, max|u|) alone.
For λ=1 and U_m, every integer s with |s|≤⌊m/2⌋ is reached from 0 by an admissible word. The explicit positive word is u=2,4,...,2n.
For λ=2 and U_m, every even 2n with |n|≤(m-1)_+ is reached from 0 by an admissible word. The explicit nonnegative word uses letters k+2 at step k.
For every finite U, the origin-reachable residual equals λℤ intersect the symmetric invariant interval.
Sign symmetry of U_m forces M(λ,U_m)=|R|/2.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the constant word of any letter of length v_3(s-t)+1 distinguishes the output streams of F_{λ,U}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u) with output lsd(s+u). Distinct residuals are therefore Mealy-inequivalent, so M(λ,U)=|R_{λ,U}| on every nonempty origin-reachable machine in this regime.
At λ=3, translation by 3k preserves every output stream: signedTrace 3 (s+3k) w = signedTrace 3 s w. This symmetry is not origin-reachable when max|u|≤1.
Some listed finite U at λ=1 or λ=2 has M(λ,U)<|R_{λ,U}|.
Identical immediate lsd signatures force behavioral equivalence of residual states.
If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, every word of length v_3(s-t)+1 distinguishes the lsd output streams of F_{λ,U}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u). A common cyclic letter is not required.
3-adic residual rigidity requires a common cyclic or constant legal letter.
Some Model A–D finite control constraint merges distinct residuals at the same control state.
At λ=3, translation by 3k preserves the output stream of every word, so a control-language restriction cannot destroy that symmetry.
If 3^L divides s-t and |w|≤L, then the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} from s and t agree on w. A remaining-horizon L controller therefore merges (s,q_L) and (t,q_L) whenever that congruence holds.
If λ is not divisible by 3, s≠t, and |w|≥v_3(s-t)+1, then the lsd streams differ on w. Finite horizon preserves residual distinguishability exactly when a legal word of that length exists.
Some legal word shorter than v_3(s-t)+1 always separates distinct residuals, even when the control language forbids every critical-length word.
Finite control horizon creates residual merges only through deadlock or empty continuation.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} agree on a word w if and only if |w|≤v_3(s-t). A finite control language therefore merges (s,q) and (t,q) exactly when every legal word is shorter than v_3(s-t)+1.
A proper subset of the complete depth-L control tree can merge residuals that some remaining word of length v_3(s-t)+1 would separate.
If F(s,c)=λ·D(s+h(c)) then F(s,(d1,d2))=λ·D(s+d1 d2). Two-trit product residual factors through the raw contribution.
For trit pairs (d1,d2) and any gain λ, λ·D(0+d1 d2)=0. Origin-reachable residual of two-trit product forcing is {0}, matching F_{λ,U_1}.
Three-trit product has a different origin-reachable residual than two-trit product.
The two-trit product machine has a 3-state origin-reachable residual.

For every realized finite Juggler word w, n^{3^{#O(w)}} = T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} + Δ_w(n), where Δ is the recursively lifted accumulation of local floor remainders. Δ ≥ 0, so the power envelope is a corollary; Δ = 0 iff every local remainder vanishes; concatenation is the two-term power-gap lift, not an additive sum.

For a realized Juggler word w, the first positive local remainder sits after a tight even or odd power-of-two prefix. That remainder contributes at least ρ_j^{2^j} to Δ, and the suffix operator Amplify (later remainders dropped) is a lower bound. An odd letter lifts an inserted defect by the exact cubic (x^a+D)^3-x^{3a} ≥ 3 x^{2a} D. Mixed OOE has firstDefect ≤ 1, with Δ ≥ 3 T(n)^4 ρ_0 or Δ ≥ ρ_1^2. These bounds do not claim Δ exceeds the formal surplus.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the relative slack 1+q = n^{3^{#O(w)}} / T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} multiplies under concatenation: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{3^{#O(v)}} (1+q_v)^{2^{|u|}}. An even letter multiplies by (1+η)^{2^k}; an odd letter multiplies by (1+q)^3 (1+η)^{2^k}. Running 1+q does not decrease under a realized extension. The surplus ratio R=Δ/S satisfies R≤1 iff T_w(n)≥n whenever S>0, so R is the endpoint comparison in other coordinates. A realized return T_w(n)=n uses the whole formal surplus.

Two consecutive persistent expanding Juggler residual blocks are impossible. Counterexample: 365 follows OOE to 763 and 763 follows OOE to 1749; both steps are PersistentExpandingResidual. An expanding O^a E^b block has a≥2, and a persistent residual endpoint is odd-to-odd so the next residual also has a≥2; that state is compatible with another expanding block. The n≤80 contracting sequels at 37 and 69 are a small-window artifact.

The integer exponent surplus of a finite Juggler word is E(w)=3^{#O(w)}-2^{|w|}, and E(w)>0 if and only if the itinerary is formally expanding. An expanding residual block O^a E^b with b≥1 has b<a. On an expanding itinerary, n^{3^{#O}}=n^{2^{|w|}+E(w)}. Relative slack multiplies under concatenation, and the slack numerator of a three-block word is n^{3^{o(v)+o(w)}}. The chain 365 --OOE--> 763 --OOE--> 1749 --OOE--> 4447 is a PersistentExpansionChain. This does not bound consecutive expanding persistent runs.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the pair (A,B)=(3^{#O(w)}, 2^{|w|}) multiplies under concatenation, and n^A = T_w(n)^B + Δ_w(n). The 1+q concatenation law is the same identity in multiplier coordinates: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{A_v} (1+q_v)^{B_u}. In logarithms this is log T = λ log n - c and the weighted cocycle y_m = Λ_m y_0 - C_m with B_m = C_m/Λ_m. The local comparison c < (λ-1) log n is T_w(n) > n on an expanding itinerary. These are the existing slack identities, not a new obstruction.

Four consecutive persistent expanding Juggler residual blocks exist: 1999 follows OOE to 5169, 5169 follows OOOOEE to 50093, 50093 follows OOE to 193753, and 193753 follows OOE to 887471. Each step is PersistentExpandingResidual.

Positive local slack, after the exact expansion weights, puts a nontrivial upper bound on the density or run length of expanding persistent residual blocks independently of T_w(n)≥n. In particular there is a uniform ε>0 with c/(λ-1)≥ε on every expanding persistent block, or the normalized budget B_m is bounded below independently of the endpoint tautology B_m≤y_0(1-1/Λ_m). Counterexamples: the OOE block at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}; B_m/B_taut reaches 10^{-9} on the n≤4000 window; a length-5 all-expanding persistent run starts at 2183.

The local Juggler remainder satisfies 0≤ρ<2T+1, hence η=ρ/T^2 < 2/T + 1/T^2 and 1+η < ((T+1)/T)^2. For the mixed itinerary OOE, 1+q = (1+η0)^3 (1+η1)^2 (1+η2)^4, and 1+q is strictly below the successor-ratio product ((T0+1)/T0)^6 ((T1+1)/T1)^4 ((T2+1)/T2)^8. The same bound at a successor start y depends only on the itinerary of y.

On realized odd-odd OOE starts, the last even remainder dominates the relative slack, and q_OOE(n) has order n^{-9/8}. After 329 follows OOOOOOOOE to y≈1.80·10^{32}, the next OOE block has 0<q<10^{-30} with q/y^{-9/8}≈2.64. Persistent expanding pairs have OOE-sequel q2 tracking y^{-9/8}. Large λ reduces successor q only by inflating y.

If a realized mixed itinerary has q_w(n)→0 then the itinerary converges to an exact rigid monochrome tower. Counterexample: the mixed itinerary OOE at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}. Exact equality rigidity has no naive quantitative stability theorem.

A residual-shaped word O^a E^b is formally expanding iff 2^{a+b}<3^a. For a≥1 this is equivalent to a+b ≤ log₂(3^a), or b ≤ maxExpandingEvens(a). In particular a=2 or 3 forces b≤1, and a=4 forces b≤2. This is the syntactic expanding language, not a realized-orbit theorem.

For n≥2, PersistentOddResidual x y if and only if PersistentExpandingResidual x y. A contracting residual cannot overshoot, and 2^k=3^o is impossible for a nonempty residual. The expanding qualifier of a persistent residual is therefore redundant.

The expanding residual word grammar, or a finite residue-mod-8 successor automaton, is an independent obstruction to an infinite persistent expanding chain. Counterexamples: on n≥2 persistence already is expansion, so the attack reduces to T_w(n)>n; the OOE type self-loop 365→763→1749 exits odd-to-even at 4447; every odd class modulo 8 both continues and leaves the PE frontier. A finite run bound M is not proved and is not supplied by this grammar.

T(x)=m if and only if m²≤F(x)<(m+1)², with F(x)=x on the even branch and F(x)=x³ on the odd branch. The landing gap ρ=F(x)-m² satisfies 0≤ρ<2T(x)+1. Odd landing is membership of F(x) in a union of odd-m one-step preimages. These are the existing inverse-floor and remainder-window lemmas under landing names.

The normalized landing position θ=ρ/(2T+1) is a compact state for persistent odd-to-odd continuation: it occupies a proper subinterval of [0,1], or a coarse θ-bin predicts the next landing parity better than a residue class, or θ(T(x)) is a function of θ(x) and the branch. Counterexamples: on odd n≤2000, odd-odd θ occupies [0,0.997] and every tenth of [0,1]; PE-continuation landings span [0,0.995]; next-parity entropy given a θ-bin is ≈0.99, matching x mod 8; θ→θ transitions fill essentially all bins.
If x is odd, T(x)=y is odd, and ρ=x³-y² is the local odd remainder, then ρ is even. This is the opposite parity of peakOddDefect_odd, which requires an even maximum.

On a realized OO word with z=T(T(x)), the sequential defect Γ=x⁹-z⁴ equals globalDefect(x,[odd,odd]). The two-step polynomial (x³-ρ)³=(z²+σ)² is y⁶=y⁶. These are the existing OO slack identity and the local floor identities under sequential names.

The peak slack identity x³=(p^{2^r}+ε)²+δ, which requires an even maximum M, transports to a persistent odd-odd pair. Counterexamples: on every odd-odd start n≤2000, including the residual chain 365, 763, 1749, the landing y=T(x) is odd, so peakOddDefect_odd does not apply and peakOddDefect(x,y) is even.

If y is odd and T(y) is odd, then the local remainder ρ=y³-T(y)² satisfies ρ≡y-1 (mod 8). Consequently v₂(ρ)=1 when y≡3 or 7 (mod 8), v₂(ρ)=2 when y≡5 (mod 8), and v₂(ρ)≥3 when y≡1 (mod 8) and ρ≠0. The same congruences hold for any odd square below y³; the floor T(y)=⌊y^{3/2}⌋ is not used beyond selecting an odd landing.

Persistent-expanding residual history forces a 2-adic landing restriction stronger than y mod 8: either v₂(y³-T(y)²)≥r>1 at a PE endpoint, or y≡1 (mod 16) forces v₂≥4, or the valuation locks the next residual word. Counterexamples: 365 maps to the PE endpoint 763 with v₂=1; 33≡1 (mod 16) has v₂=3; on odd n≤4000 the PE valuation table is the residue law, and v₂=1 continues as both persistent OOE and non-persistent OOEE.

y=T_w(x) with x realising w if and only if follows x w and image x w = y. Each letter is the existing inverse-floor cell: T(n)=m iff m²≤F(n)<(m+1)² with F(n)=n on the even branch and F(n)=n³ on the odd branch. These are the itinerary and cell lemmas under cylinder names.

The predecessor cylinder of a persistent-expanding residual word constrains T(y) mod 2 or the next residual grammar in a way invisible from y, y mod 8, or θ(y). Counterexamples: 3461 maps under OOE to 9585 with T even and 3803 maps under OOE to 10657 with T odd; both endpoints are 1 mod 8 with θ≈0.382. On expanding overshoots n≤4000 every PE word with at least 8 samples realises both next parities.

Write oddLanding y for y odd and T(y) odd, and oddRun 0 y = oddLanding y, oddRun (r+1) y = oddLanding y and oddRun r (T(y)). Then oddRun (r+1) y if and only if y is odd and oddRun r (T(y)). The odd-landing cylinder of a fixed m contains at most one integer.

The iterated odd-landing sets P_r occupy shrinking arithmetic cylinders, or iteration is recognized modulo 2^m, or successive square-gap coordinates on long odd runs are constrained. Counterexamples: on odd n≤8000 the stay fraction |P_{r+1}|/|P_r| is 0.49–0.53 through r=7; P_r is mostly isolated odds; every residue modulo 64 both continues and exits; θ on P_r and on the exit from P_{r-1} both occupy [0,1].

For every natural n and finite parity itinerary w, follows n w if and only if the actual length-|w| Juggler itinerary of n equals w. The itinerary image equals the |w|-fold iterate, and images and realization compose under word concatenation.
If n and m realize the same finite Juggler word w and n ≤ m, then the image of n after w is at most the image of m after w.
For every finite Juggler word w realized at n, J^{|w|}(n)^{2^{|w|}} ≤ n^{3^{#O(w)}}. If n ≥ 2 and 3^{#O(w)} < 2^{|w|}, then J^{|w|}(n) < n.

The even fiber J(n)=m is the parity-restricted square interval m² ≤ n < (m+1)², while the odd fiber is the parity-restricted cube-to-square interval m² ≤ n³ < (m+1)²; any odd fiber contains at most one integer.

Every nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ≥ 2 is formally expanding. Cycle extrema satisfy the certified parity, order, square-scale, and nested-cell constraints; a minimum-based cycle orientation cannot end in an odd letter. The path from a cycle minimum to any later even state is superquadratic. These are necessary cycle restrictions, not an exclusion of all cycles.

For S_O(N) = sum over odd n ≤ N of (-1)^{floor(n^{3/2})}, the exact fractional-part formulation together with the classical van der Corput and Erdős–Turán inequalities gives |S_O(N)| ≪ N^{5/6}. This is an ambient odd-input bound, not a Juggler-orbit transfer theorem.

The odd-to-odd Juggler starts have natural density 1/4. Equivalently, the starts that admit a uniform one- or two-step FiniteProgress certificate (every even start n ≥ 2, and every odd start whose first image is even) have natural density 3/4. This is the counting corollary |OO(N)-N/4| ≪ N^{5/6} of the ambient odd-input discrepancy bound. It is a density of that uniform short-certificate class, not of all FiniteProgress, not of ReachesOne, and not a Lean counting theorem.

Universal FiniteProgress for starts above one implies universal reachability of one. Every even start n ≥ 2 and every odd start n ≥ 2 whose first image is even has FiniteProgress; consequently, any start without FiniteProgress is odd and has an odd first image. This isolates the automatic odd-to-odd frontier without proving universal progress.

Neither OOOEOE nor OOOOEE is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2 (Paper A Lemma 3.5). The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 256 together with the last-even one-step preimage against the coarse lower envelope n^{81} > 2^{130}(n+1)^{64} for n ≥ 256. This excludes those two orientations only; the length-≤6 census is the separate row J-small-cycle-census.

No itinerary of length at most six is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least seven (Paper A Theorem 3.6). Assembly: rotation invariance of cycle itineraries, exclusion of all-odd itineraries by strict odd ascent, rotation to an even-terminating orientation, the formal-expansion filter, the next-square thresholds of Lemma 3.4, the leftover exclusions of OOOEOE and OOOOEE (Lemma 3.5; rotation targets of OEOOOE and EOOOOE). Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_six. Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-seven; this row is the length-≤6 statement only. This is not an exclusion of all cycles and not a halt theorem.

Neither OOOOEOE nor OOOOOEE is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2 (Paper A Lemma 3.7). The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 14 together with the last-even one-step preimage against the coarse lower envelope n^{243} > 2^{422}(n+1)^{128} for n ≥ 14. This excludes those two orientations only; the length-≤7 census is the separate row J-small-cycle-census-seven.

No itinerary of length at most seven is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least eight (Paper A Theorem 3.8). Assembly: the length-≤6 census, the formal-expansion filter on length seven, the odd-run exclusion of O^6E, the internal-E bootstrap exclusions of OOEOOOE and OOOEOOE, rotation of EOOOOOE and OEOOOOE onto the leftovers, and the leftover exclusions of OOOOEOE and OOOOOEE (Lemma 3.7). Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_seven. Strengthened by Paper A Theorem 3.22 / Corollary 3.23 (even-count at most three is impossible, so the period is at least eleven). This is not an exclusion of all cycles and not a halt theorem.

No itinerary of length at most eight is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least nine. Assembly: the length-≤7 census, the formal-expansion filter on length eight, the odd-run exclusion of O^7E, Theorem 3.12 at k=8, rotation of EOOOOOOE and OEOOOOOE onto those leftovers, and the internal-E bootstrap exclusions of OOOOEOOE, OOOEOOOE, and OOEOOOOE. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_eight in LengthEightCensus.lean. Implied by Paper A Corollary 3.23 (period at least eleven). Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-ten. This is not a length-9 itinerary census and not a halt theorem.

If a Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ends with r ≥ 1 even letters, the state immediately before that trailing even run is strictly less than (n+1)^{2^r}. The case r = 1 is the last-even one-step preimage; r = 2 is the two-even bound of Paper A Lemma 3.5 on OOOOEE; r = 3 is the three-even bound for OOOOOOEEE. Lean theorem cycle_trailing_evens_lt. This is a one-step-preimage identity, not a leftover exclusion and not a halt theorem.

OOOOOOEEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2. The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 128 together with the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against the coarse lower envelope n^{729} > 2^{1330}(n+1)^{512} for n ≥ 128. The computational prefix-cell first fires at N0 = 73; 128 is the algebraic cutoff. This excludes that one three-even leftover only; it is not a length-9 census, not an exclusion of the remaining eight leftovers, and not a halt theorem. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_ooooooeee.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the even-terminating two-even leftover O^{k-2}EE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Large n uses the shared tail n^{3^{k-2}} > 2^{e_{k-2}}(n+1)^{2^k} at the uniform algebraic cutoff n ≥ 256, obtained by cubing the length-6 comparison; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a) = log2(lowerDenom(O^a)). Below 256 the argument is the existing k=6,7 leftovers, a Fin 256 table at k=8, and the fact that n ≥ 2 does not follow seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_two_even_ee. This excludes that one family only; it is not a length-8 census and not a halt theorem.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the leftover O^{k-3}EOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. The last-odd cube trick plus (y+1)^3 < 2(n+1)^4 reduces to the same shared tail as O^{k-2}EE. Large n is n ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is the existing k=6,7 leftovers, Fin 256 tables at k=8,9, and the seven-odd obstruction for k ≥ 10. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_two_even_eoe. This excludes that one family only; it is not a length-8 census and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 4, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EE is not a Juggler CycleMin at n. CycleMin puts the remainder O^b EE at y = T_{O^a E}(n) ≥ n. The leftover cell is measured against n, so y ≥ n tightens it against the shared two-even tail at y. Large y is the uniform cutoff y ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is seven consecutive odds on the prefix or the remainder, or a Fin 256 table on the short-gap window 2 ≤ a ≤ 6, 4 ≤ b ≤ 6. Lean theorem no_cycleMin_gapped_three_even_ee. This excludes gapped CycleMins only; it is not a CycleItinerary theorem at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail attack, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 3, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EOE is not a Juggler CycleMin at n. The same first-E transport applies: y ≥ n tightens the leftover cell against the shared two-even tail at y, using the last-odd cube reduction already used for O^{k-3}EOE. Large y is y ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is seven-odd or a Fin 256 table on 2 ≤ a ≤ 6, 3 ≤ b ≤ 6. Lean theorem no_cycleMin_gapped_three_even_eoe. This excludes gapped CycleMins only; it is not a CycleItinerary theorem at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail attack, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Large n uses the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against C_{O^a}, which is the tail n^{3^a} > 2^{e_a}(n+1)^{2^{a+3}} at the algebraic cutoff n ≥ 128, obtained by cubing the OOOOOOEEE comparison; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a) = log2(lowerDenom(O^a)). Below 128 the argument is the existing a=6 table and the fact that n ≥ 2 does not follow seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eee. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not the other six bunched tails, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 5 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 4 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^6: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the one-odd envelope gives y^3 ≤ 4p^2, and n ≥ 4 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^3. Large n at a = 5 uses the tail n^{3^a} > 2^{e_a}(n+1)^{6·2^a} at the algebraic cutoff n ≥ 314, obtained by persisting the comparison at 314 and cubing in a; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a). At a = 6 the same cell already fires at n ≥ 16. Below those cutoffs the argument is the a = 5 table, the a = 6 table, and seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eoee. This excludes that one bunched family only; a uniform coarse (n+1)^K cell for all six remaining bunched families is false; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 4 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 32 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the two-odd envelope gives y^9 ≤ 1024 p^4, and n ≥ 32 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^2. The resulting comparison is the shared two-even tail at length a+2, which holds for n ≥ 256. Below 256 the argument is Fin 256 tables at a = 4,5,6 and seven consecutive odds thereafter. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eooee. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 3 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOOOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For a ≥ 4 and n ≥ 3 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the three-odd envelope gives y^{27} ≤ 2^{38} p^8, and n ≥ 3 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^2. The resulting comparison is the shared two-even tail at length a+2, which holds for n ≥ 256. At a = 3 the coarse exponent is impossible, so the argument uses the tight cell z < (y+1)^2 against C_{O^3}: y < 39 contradicts n ≥ 24, and y ≥ 39 reduces to n^{729} > 2^{1650}(n+1)^{512} from n ≥ 197. Below 256 the argument is Fin 256 tables at a = 3,4,5,6 and seven consecutive odds thereafter. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eoooee. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 5 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EEOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 4 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^6: the last-odd cube gives y^3 < (n+1)^4, two leading evens give z < (y+1)^4, and n ≥ 4 upgrades that to z < (n+1)^6. The resulting comparison is the EOEE tail n^{3^a} > 2^{e_a}(n+1)^{6·2^a}, already proved for a ≥ 5. Large n at a = 5 is n ≥ 314; at a = 6 the same cell already fires at n ≥ 16. Below those cutoffs the argument is the a = 5 table, the a = 6 table, and seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eeoe. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 4 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOEOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 32 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: the last-odd cube gives y^3 < (n+1)^4, the one-odd envelope on the first gap upgrades to w < (n+1)^2, and the even cell at z then gives z < (n+1)^4. The resulting comparison is the shared two-even tail at length a+2, which holds for n ≥ 256. Below 256 the argument is Fin 256 tables at a = 4,5,6 and seven consecutive odds thereafter. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eoeoe. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 3 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOOEOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For a ≥ 4 and n ≥ 4 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: last-odd plus two-odd give u^9 < 1024(y+1)^8 and (y+1)^3 < 2(n+1)^4, hence u^{27} < 2^{38}(n+1)^{32} and u < (n+1)^2. The resulting comparison is the shared two-even tail at length a+2, which holds for n ≥ 256. At a = 3 the same tight split as O^3 EOOOEE applies with u in place of y. Below 256 the argument is Fin 256 tables at a = 3,4,5,6 and seven consecutive odds thereafter. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eooeoe. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 4, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Every CycleItinerary has a CycleMin rotation. The k=0 rotation is the first-E CycleMin exclusion; the rotation at k=a+1 is the bootstrap itinerary O^b EE O^a E, excluded by last-gap ≥ 2 (OOO at N=3, or OO at N=5 with n=3 failing to follow four odds); the last even starts even; every other rotation ends odd. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_gapped_three_even_ee. This upgrades the CycleMin theorem to CycleItinerary; it is not first-E transport at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail theorem, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 3, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. The same rotation classes apply: first-E CycleMin at k=0; bootstrap O^b EOE O^a E at k=a+1 (last-gap ≥ 2, with n=3 and b=3 failing after OOOE at 6); start OE at k=a+b+2; every other rotation ends odd. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_gapped_three_even_eoe. This upgrades the CycleMin theorem to CycleItinerary; it is not first-E transport at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail theorem, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

No n ≥ 2 realizes a Juggler cycle itinerary with at most three even letters (Paper A Theorem 3.22). Every CycleItinerary has a CycleMin rotation that starts OO, ends E, and is formally expanding; those itineraries are the odd-run family, the two-even leftovers (Theorem 3.12), the internal-E bootstrap, the seven bunched leftovers (Theorems 3.14–3.20), or the gapped leftovers (Theorems 3.13 and 3.21). The corollary is that a nontrivial cycle itinerary has length at least eleven (Paper A Corollary 3.23). Lean theorems no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three and cycle_itinerary_length_ge_eleven in EvenCountThree.lean. This is an even-count assembler, not a length-9 or length-10 itinerary census, and not a halt theorem.

No cycle itinerary with cycle minimum at least 300 has fewer than eight even letters, so a nontrivial cycle has period at least twenty-two (Paper A Theorem 3.31). Every n ≤ 299 reaches 1. The e ≤ 7 census enumerates 16 + 186 + 2037 + 25353 + 325452 canonical forms and closes them by the sharp run-suffix law of Theorem 3.29; the last family closes at n ≥ 64. Theorem 3.22 remains the floor-free Lean bound (e ≥ 4, period ≥ 11 for every n ≥ 2). Enumeration in run_suffix_law.closure; not Lean and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 follows the Juggler word O^7, then T^7(n) ≥ (n+1)^16. In particular the EEEE inverse cell [n^16, (n+1)^16) is empty of seven-odd images, so O^7 EEEE is not a cycle itinerary. Lean theorems o7_image_ge_succ_pow16 and no_cycle_itinerary_oooooooeeee in O7EEEEGap.lean. Proof: no_follows_seven_odds_of_lt256 excludes n < 256; on an O^7 run the exact cells x_k^3 < (x_{k+1}+1)^2 and x_k ≥ n compose to n^{6177} < (n+1)^{3990} (T^7(n)+1)^{128}; for n ≥ 256 one has n^{6177} > (n+1)^{6038} because 257^{256} < 3·256^{256} and 256^{139} > 2^{40} > 3^{24} > (257/256)^{6038}. This replaces the leftover 4-fudge (first fire at 828484409) by the exact successor cell. Not a length-11 census and not a halt theorem. Imported by JugglerPaper (Paper A Lemma 3.28).

No n ≥ 3 realizes the Juggler cycle itinerary O^7 EEEE. On 3 ≤ n < 828484409 the seven-odd image never enters the EEEE inverse cell [n^16, (n+1)^16): 6473954 O^7 starts, 3234088 even images, all strictly above the cell, closest ratio T^7(n)/(n+1)^16 = 445.01 at n=289. For n ≥ 828484409 the leftover prefix-cell n^{3^7} > 2^{denomBits(7)} (n+1)^{2^{11}} forbids a return. This is a one-word empty-window scan, not a Lean theorem, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

On a MinimalNonTerm or CycleMin start, the first even residual always overshoots: T(O^a E)(n) > n and the even residual sits at or above (n+1)^2. The return-to-n cell of the first-even dichotomy is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary, now excluded by no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three. Lean theorems minimal_first_even_overshoots and cycleMin_first_even_overshoots in EvenCountThree.lean. This sharpens the leftover start. It is not a four-even exclusion, not a halt theorem, and not a ReturnBelow law.

For odd n ≥ 3 with m = floor(n^{3/2}): m^{3/2} = (3/2) m n^{3/4} - (1/2) n^{9/4} + E(n) with 0 ≤ E(n) ≤ (3/8)(n^{3/2}-1)^{-1/2} ≤ (1/2) n^{-3/4}. Substituting theta = n^{3/2} - m into the linear Taylor term eliminates the nested fractional part exactly; the integer m enters the phase linearly with smooth amplitude. Companion gap lemma: m(n+2h) - m(n) = floor(delta) + [ {n^{3/2}} ≥ 1 - {delta} ] with delta = (n+2h)^{3/2} - n^{3/2}, giving constant-gap cells of length about n^{1/2}/h. Both validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}.

Paper B Corollary 4.6 (9 September 2026 repair), taking a marginal: each joint parity class of (floor(n^(3/2)), floor(floor(n^(3/2))^(3/2))) over odd n <= N has count N/8 + O(N^(23/24) log(2N)^3). Theorem 4.5 gives a replacement small-shift proof, including mixed signs and zero frequencies. Ambient counting, not an orbit-frequency or termination theorem; the old general decorated kernel is not used.

For odd n ≥ 3 with m = floor(n^{3/2}) and v = floor(m^{3/2}): v^{1/2} = n^{9/8} + D(n) with -(3/4) n^{-3/8} - n^{-9/8} ≤ D(n) ≤ 0, where D(n) = -(3/4) theta n^{-3/8} - (1/2) theta_2 m^{-3/4} - E_3 - E_2 by two applications of the linearization pattern of row J-nested-parity-linearization. Every non-smooth term has decaying amplitude, so smoothing the fourth-letter phase (k/2) v^{1/2} to (k/2) n^{9/8} costs only O(k N^{5/8}) cumulatively. Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic through n = 10^{12}, worst ratio 0.9970 against supremum 1.

Paper B Corollary 4.6 (9 September 2026 repair): for m=floor(n^(3/2)), v=floor(m^(3/2)), each of the eight sign classes ((-1)^m, (-1)^v, (-1)^floor(sqrt(v))) over odd n <= N has count N/16 + O(N^(23/24) log(2N)^3). The third coordinate is the formal even branch; this is not the complete depth-four itinerary census. Theorem 4.5 and a pointwise square-root comparison prove the result.

Unconditional Paper B Theorem 5.2 (9 September 2026 repair): the starts admitting a power-envelope descent certificate of length at most four have count 13N/16 + O(N^(23/24) log(2N)^3). The disjoint minimal prefixes are E, OE, OOEE. Corollary 4.6 proves the previously missing OOEE correlation. This sufficient certificate class need not exhaust every start descending within four operations; it is not a termination theorem.

Second-order exact linearization (Lemma G): for odd n ≥ 5 with X = n^{3/2}, m = floor(X): m^{3/4} = (5/32) n^{9/8} + (15/16) m n^{-3/8} - (3/32) m^2 n^{-15/8} - R3 with 0 ≤ R3 ≤ (5/128)(X-1)^{-9/4}, and m^{9/4} = (5/32) n^{27/8} - (9/16) m n^{15/8} + (45/32) m^2 n^{3/8} + R4 with -(15/128)(X-1)^{-3/4} ≤ R4 ≤ 0, by Taylor to third order with the exact substitution theta = X - m in both the linear and quadratic terms. Consequently (Proposition H) the OOO* layer phase v^{3/2}, v = floor(m^{3/2}), equals a degree-(2,1) polynomial in the integer pair (m, v) with smooth coefficients, up to an error of at most (3/4) n^{-9/8}. The integer m enters quadratically with smooth coefficients and decaying remainders — the algebraic brick for the tier-2 (second growing layer) discrepancy attack. Validated by exact scaled-integer arithmetic (scale 10^{60}) through n = 10^{12}. The tier-2 discrepancy bound was subsequently proved (row J-kernel-cancellation, Theorem R).

Conditional implication (Proposition J): if for every itinerary word w of length d the class count satisfies |#w(N) - 2^{-d} N| ≤ E_d(N), then the starts with no contracting prefix of length ≤ d number at most (N_d/2^d) N + N_d E_d(N), where N_d counts the length-d words with no contracting prefix. That count is exact: 3^{o_t} ≥ 2^t must hold at every t ≤ d and depends on nothing but (t, o_t), so N_d is a dynamic program over the triangle 0 ≤ o ≤ t ≤ d, in integers. The closed form N_d ≤ 2^d e^{-cd} with c = 2 (log2/log3 - 1/2)^2 > 0.0342 follows by dropping every constraint but t = d and applying Hoeffding to the odd-letter count (o_d ≥ d log2/log3); that closed form is what this row carried until 2026-09-05, and it is lossy by 6.7 at d = 5, 43.6 at d = 40 and 1.3e4 at d = 1600. The loss is not in the rate -- the sharp value is -log rho = 0.034688 against Hoeffding's 0.034285, one part in eighty -- but polynomial: N_d/2^d ~ C rho^d d^{-3/2} with C about 11, the d^{-1/2} for staying nonnegative under the zero-drift tilt and a further d^{-1} because the tilted endpoint sits at height ~sqrt(d) rather than at the origin. Every other start n ≥ 2 has a uniform power-envelope descent certificate within d steps (row J-power-envelope-contraction). Hence all-depth parity equidistribution with power savings (Conjecture K; proved unconditionally for all itineraries of length ≤ 4 — rows J-triple-parity-discrepancy, J-even-branch-third-letter, J-depth4-slow-branch, J-depth4-complete; depth ≥ 5 open) implies that the set of Juggler starts admitting a finite descent certificate has natural density one — the Juggler analogue of the Terras program. E-rooted words have a contracting prefix at length 1, so only O-rooted class bounds are ever consumed. The implication is unconditional; the hypothesis is open beyond the proved cases. Not a termination claim; no unconditional density-one claim. Imported into the finite-dynamics note as Proposition 6.1. The exact count at d = 5 has four survivors -- OOOOO, OOOOE, OOOEO, OOEOO -- hence certificate density 1 - 4/32 = 7/8, which is Paper B Corollary 6.4's figure reached by counting words rather than contractors; d = 6 is 7/8 again, since all eight children survive.

Rate-free and biased-split reductions of the density-one hypothesis. (A) If for each FIXED depth d every parity class w of length d satisfies #w(N) = 2^{-d} N + o(N) as N -> infinity (qualitative, no rate, non-uniform in d), then the set of Juggler starts with a finite descent certificate has natural density one: Proposition J's inequality (row J-equidistribution-implies-density-one) #(no contracting prefix <= d) <= (N_d/2^d) N + N_d E_d(N), with N -> infinity taken BEFORE d -> infinity, gives upper density <= N_d/2^d for every d (and <= e^{-cd} via the closed form); certificates are the Lean power envelope (power_bound_word: an exponent-negative prefix 3^{a_k} < 2^k forces x_k <= n^{3^a/2^k} < n). Proposition CC: no family-averaging method (double large sieve, dispersion, amplification over the mode index k) can by itself bound the depth-5 class count. Proposition 7.4 of the parity-discrepancy paper (shift-averaged L^2 bound; formerly 'Lemma II' with an overquantified corollary, corrected in Phase 26): let A_1 < ... < A_L be reals with |A_t - A_t'| >= A'_min |t - t'| for some A'_min >= 1 and let x_1, ..., x_L be arbitrary reals. Corrected consequence via Markov: |S_lambda| <= sqrt((L/eps)(1 + (6/pi)(log L + 1)/A'_min)) outside a shift set of measure <= eps — square-root cancellation times sqrt(log L) in general, genuine square-root only when A'_min >> log L (true in the level-3 instance, A'_min ~ P^{11/16}). The former 'in particular |S_lambda| <= sqrt(L/eps) off measure eps(1+o(1))' was false as quantified (the exceptional measure carried an O(log L) factor). The average says nothing about the single shift lambda = 0; it does not make the level-3 kernel 'generically cancelling' in any sense bearing on Conjecture 7.3. Validated by shift_average_probe (mean R = 1.0042 at P = 10^6, 0.9961 at P = 10^8).

HH at lambda = 0 is a specific-point-in-metric-theory problem (the 'is sqrt(2) normal' species); the instance's special arithmetic A^2 = (9/16) k^2 z re-enters the harmonic toolkit via its known exploitations. Third and final layer of the K3 obstruction (after BB, GG); the K3/HH line is PARKED here.

Exact short-cluster closure T_{O^b E O^c E}(y) = n forces an impossible defect equation: a tiny gap z^3 = n^4 + delta, a wrong parity, or a finite algebraic signature that CycleMin prefixes cannot meet. Mal'cev reduction to the fundamental domain [0,1)^3 yields the vertical chi_Δ = {-A ΔB - ΔA floor(ΔB)} = {-A(n+h) floor(ΔB) - A(n){ΔB}}. The first summand is integer dilation of {A(n+h)} (cheap A-axis). The second is the amplitude-product A{ΔB} with A ≍ n^{9/8} and A(n+2)-A(n) ~ (27/8) n^{1/8} >> 1 (GG species). Equivalently A{ΔB} is the vertical of a second Heisenberg lift of (A(n), ΔB(n,h), 0) — the same group law as J-tower-heisenberg-coordinate, not a degree drop to a published Hardy-nil orbit. The leftover of ΔB against (n+h)^{9/4}-n^{9/4} has size ≍ n^{3/4}, so the difference is not o(1)-close to a Hardy-in-n pair. This is a different identity from the v94 abelian difference {v(n+h)^{9/4}-v(n)^{9/4}}. Consequence: characteristic-factor / PET induction cannot keep the floor-removal correction as a coordinate through the first step. The rate-free conjecture is unharmed (Leibman on the horizontal remains the unbuilt composition). Not a K3 bound and not a Paper B edit.

There is an ineffective X_0 such that for every X >= X_0 and every interval I of consecutive odd integers contained in [X, 2X] with |I| = floor((2/3) X^{1/3}), the values floor(x^{3/2}) for x in I are not all of one parity. This is Paper B Lemmas 3.2–3.4 (parity bridge, van der Corput second-derivative, Erdős–Turán) localized to the hug-flow working window: g(r) = (1/2)(2r+1)^{3/2} has g'' ≍ X^{-1/2} uniformly on the dyadic block, the h-th mode is ≪ H h^{1/2} X^{-1/4} + h^{-1/2} X^{1/4}, and cutoff K = X^{1/6} gives absolute discrepancy D ≪ X^{1/6} + X^{1/4} = o(H). No resonance exclusion is used (first-derivative locking lengthens sojourns but does not shrink g''). Not a depth-2 statement, not C_L nonempty, not a transfer theorem, not a Paper B edit, and not a halt theorem.

For every odd integer x ≥ 3, floor((x+2)^{3/2}) − floor(x^{3/2}) ≥ 3 floor(√x). Proof: (x+2)^{3/2} > x^{3/2}+3√x because (x+2)^3 − (x^{3/2}+3√x)^2 = 3x+8 > 0, hence the floor difference is at least floor(3√x) ≥ 3 floor(√x). At image scale Y = floor(x^{3/2}) the depth-1 working window is (2/3) Y^{1/3} ≤ (2/3)√x, so the gap exceeds that whole window (ratio → 9/2). Therefore the image V(I) of any odd window I is a 3√X-separated packing, not a consecutive interval, and interval Erdős–Turán cannot be applied to y = floor(x^{3/2}). Not a depth-2 mixing theorem, not C_L nonempty, not a Paper B edit, and not a halt theorem.

Gap transfer (Paper A Theorem 4.10). On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of length L and oddCount o, n · log n · min(o log 3 − L log 2, 1) ≤ 2 L (cycleMin_gap_transfer). Proof: Theorem 4.4 reads P(A − B) ≤ L A with A = 3^o, B = 2^L, P = n log n; if A ≤ B the left side is nonpositive, if A ≥ 2B then P ≤ 2L, and if B < A < 2B then Λ = log(A/B) ≤ (A − B)/B and P(A − B)/B ≤ LA/B ≤ 2L. Abstract form cycleMin_length_of_gap: any ε ≤ min(Λ, 1) gives n log n · ε ≤ 2L. Floor-free; the classical transcendence input is a hypothesis, not a Lean theorem. Not a halt theorem and not a period bound at any floor.

Short-cycle reduction (Paper A Corollary 4.11). Rhin's effective measure in the packaged form of Simons–de Weger Lemma 12, Λ = o log 3 − L log 2 > e^{−13.3(0.46057 + log L)} = e^{−6.1256} L^{−13.3} (H = max(L, o) = L on a cycle itinerary), fed into cycleMin_length_of_gap gives for every nontrivial Juggler cycle n log n ≤ 2 e^{6.1256} L^{14.3} < 915 L^{14.3}. Not a halt theorem and not a claim in the long regime.

The Juggler conjecture as an almost-all statement (fate-contagion note, Corollary 4.5). Fix N_0 with [1, N_0] ⊆ R (Lean N_0 = 260, reachesOne_of_lt_two_hundred_sixty_one; certified N_0 = 3.5·10^8). The following are equivalent: (1) every n ≥ 1 reaches 1; (2) Σ_{n ≤ x, n ∉ R} 1/n = o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ** = 0.4926…; (3) the starts n ≤ x whose orbit never enters [1, N_0] have logarithmic count o((log x)^λ) for some λ < λ**. In natural-density terms (3) asks that all but O(x (log x)^{−0.508}) starts below x eventually fall below N_0 — a Tao-type almost-bounded-values statement with a bounded target and a mild logarithmic rate. For Collatz the analogous implication fails because preimage trees are thin (Krasikov–Lagarias x^{0.84}); for the Juggler map the even preimage interval makes fates contagious. This is a reduction, not a proof of termination, and no almost-all statement of type (3) is proved.

Odd generation of two-way closed fate classes (fate-contagion note, Theorem 6.1). Fate classes are forward-closed as well as backward-closed (ForwardClosed; reachesOne_forwardClosed, not_reachesOne_forwardClosed, escapes_forwardClosed; mem_iff_floorPower_mem). For a class A that is closed both ways with 1 ∉ A: every member n ≥ 1 descends by even steps only to an odd member of A (exists_odd_ancestor: ∃ k with floorPower^[k] n odd and in A, all earlier iterates even), that member is ≥ 3 (exists_odd_ancestor_ge_three), the odd members are exactly the odd preimages of A ∩ {⌊m^{3/2}⌋ : m odd} (odd_mem_iff: for odd n, A n ↔ A (Nat.sqrt (n^3))), and A is nonempty iff it contains ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ for some odd m ≥ 3 (nonempty_iff_odd_image_mem). Consequence: every positive integer reaches 1 iff no image ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ of an odd m fails to reach 1; the failure set is the E-forest over the odd preimages of F ∩ S. This is the exact skeleton of the S-fairness reformulation: the one free term of the first-letter decomposition (6.1) is the share of OO-type odd numbers whose image lies in F. Not a halt theorem.

Paper B §4.5 (Theorems 4.11–4.12, Corollary 4.13; J-parity-triple-discrepancy-localized) now proves the localized and twisted statements in full, so this production rests on a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft.

Publication review 9 September 2026: the analytic claim below is not established by Paper B and is retained only as a historical research target. The revised paper gives conditional implications, not this analytic proof. See docs/theory/paper_b_review.md. Historical target: Paper B §3.5, Lemma 4.10 and Theorems 4.11–4.12 (nested and triple parity discrepancy on sub-dyadic intervals, with a slow twist). For every ε > 0 there is P₀ such that for P ≥ P₀, every interval I ⊆ (P, 2P] of length Y ≥ P^{1/2}, every (a,b,c) ∈ {0,1}³ ∖ {0} and every slow twist g(n) = (ℓ/2) n^{9/16} with |ℓ| ≤ P^{1/24}: |Σ_{n ∈ I odd} ψ(n^{3/2})^a ψ(m^{3/2})^b ψ(v^{1/2})^c e(g(n))| ≤ Y P^{−1/24+ε} (Theorem 4.12; Theorem 4.11 is the case c = 0). Proof: Steps 1–7 of Theorems 4.4/4.7 run over I with the number of summands Y in place of P; every cost is proportional to Y except three absolute terms — the two partial end cells 5.2 (jh)^{−1/2} P^{3/8}, the pure passenger 3.8 P^{7/16}, the majorant end cells 17 P^{1/4} — which fall below Y P^{−1/24} for Y ≥ P^{1/2}; the twist survives the Weyl differencing as e(Δ_{2h} g) with total variation ≤ 0.26 P^{−5/16} over the block and is removed by one partial summation (Lemma 4.10) against the untwisted differenced sums on initial sub-intervals, whose bound is nondecreasing in the length; in the single-smooth-sum cases the twist’s curvature 0.13 P^{1/24−23/16} is dominated by powers of P. Corollary 4.13 (the OOEEE production on even blocks): for m′ ≥ 2 and I(m′) = [m′^{32/9}, (m′+1)^{32/9}), #{odd n ∈ I(m′) : word₅(n) = OOEEE, J⁵(n) = m′} = (1/16)#{odd n ∈ I(m′)} + O(|I(m′)| m′^{−4/27+ε}), via the nesting bound 0 ≤ n^{9/16} − v^{1/4} ≤ n^{−15/16}, an Erdős–Turán/Kusmin–Landau bound Y P^{−1/16} for the exceptional set, and a Vaaler expansion of the fifth letter whose modes are the slow twists. This discharges Hypothesis L of Paper C (Appendix C) to a Paper B theorem; Paper B remains a working draft. Not a halt theorem.
